pageCache.pageTitle: Ainslie Wood Primary School - Our Vision
pageCache.text:
Our Vision
At our school, we believe that everybody matters. Every child is known, valued and supported to thrive as an individual. We are committed to creating a nurturing environment where children feel safe, confident and proud of who they are.
Through aspirational learning, we inspire children to aim high, embrace challenge and develop a lifelong love of learning. Our curriculum is rich in meaningful experiences that broaden horizons and help children make sense of the world around them.
We strive to make a difference—in our school, our community and beyond. We encourage children to grow into thoughtful, responsible citizens who understand the impact they can have on others.
Our values underpin everything we do:
Together, we nurture confident, curious learners who are ready to shape their futures and contribute positively to the world.
Welcome & Introduction
Our Vision

Welcome
A school where children, belong, discover what they're capable of and experience learning beyond the classroom. Come and take a look!
At Ainslie Wood, we believe that education is a transformative journey. We hold high expectations for every child who walks through our doors, fostering an environment of aspirational learning where academic rigour meets creative curiosity. We don't just want our pupils to achieve; we want them to excel and develop the resilience needed to navigate a changing world.
However, we know that children only reach their full potential when they feel safe, seen, and valued. Our school is built on a foundation of inclusion and belonging—a place where diversity is our strength and where every individual matters. We are committed to ensuring that no child is left behind and that every voice is heard.
Which is why our Vision for Ainslie Wood is:
"When your child comes to Ainslie Wood, your family belongs to a community."
We view the relationship between home and school as a vital partnership. We are not just educating students; we are building a supportive network that champions the success of every young person in our care.
I invite you to explore our website to see how our vibrant curriculum and dedicated team create a primary experience that is as ambitious as it is inclusive. We look forward to welcoming you into our community.
Maybe even come and visit our school in person!

Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club is run by school staff and runs from 7:30am - 8:55am. The cost is £7 per child per day.
Children can arrive at any time during this window, through the breakfast club entrance (on the car park side of the school). They can have breakfast and take part in games and activities before being taken to class at the start of the day.
Please see the terms and conditions and fill in a form (download it here or ask for one at the office) if you would like to apply for a space.

Governors
Who are the Ainslie Wood Governors?
The Ainslie Wood Governing Body is made up of 9 members. Included in this count, we have:
2 Parent Governors
Meet the Governors
Chair of Governors
Our Chair was co-opted onto our Governing Body, Bruce Roberts. Bruce was elected to our governing body in March 2025. As a Vice Chair, Bruce brought an array of skills and challenges to the board, where he is now a co-opted member. Bruce uses the skills from his work in the education sector to fulfil his governor role here. As Safeguarding Governor, Bruce visits the school regularly to oversee our safeguarding systems and to make sure that everyone is being kept safe.
Local Authority Governor
Our Local Authority Governor is Sally Davies. Sally is the Senior Philanthropy Manager at the Altzheimers Society. She has previously worked as an Account Executive at KPMG and as a caseworker and Researcher for the Shadow Minister for Children and Families.
Isabel Brown is our parent governor.
I am delighted to have joined the Ainslie Wood Governing body as an elected parent governor at the end of 2025 and to have an opportunity to contribute to the community that has so warmly welcomed my family. I value the opportunity to support the school in nurturing confident, curious learners who are ready to shape their futures and contribute positively to the world.
As a Detective Sergeant in the Metropolitan Police with over 17 years’ experience, I bring strong skills in safeguarding, critical thinking, and collaboration. Most recently working with NHS mental health professionals to support vulnerable adults and young people, giving me insight into the challenges children face in today’s digital world. I have a particular interest in mental health and online safety, and I am committed to helping every child at Ainslie Wood thrive.
Co-Opted Governors
Our co-opted governors are Edward Chilton and Jack Wicks.
Ed is the Principal Educational Psychologist for the London Borough of Hackney, with over 20 years' experience across education, SEND, applied psychology and systems leadership.
Ed has served as a primary school governor before, an experience that taught him the value of engaged, collaborative governance in helping schools thrive. He is a strong believer in the power of play, relational approaches and strengths-based practice as foundations for effective education — principles he brings to his work and to his role as a co-opted governor.
He lives locally and has a daughter at the school, giving him a close and personal connection to the community as well as a professional one.
Jack says: I have been a co-opted governor at Ainslie Wood Primary School since October 2025. I am passionate about education and work as an assistant headteacher at a nearby school. My aim is to use my experience and knowledge of the field to support the school in a productive way that benefits the children, families and staff as best possible!
The person representing our staff at the Governing Body meetings is Simone Jolie.
And finally, our Headteacher. Ms Crouch sits on the Governing Body, reporting everything about the school, how we are doing and what our plans are and then answers lots of questions. She takes an automatic position on the board, but would have worked hard to be elected as she loves finding everything out about Ainslie Wood all the time.
Committees
Our full governing body meets every half term. The committees that we do have are:
Staff Pay, Finance and Headteacher Performance.

pageCache.text:
Inclusion - including Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
Welcome
We know that children learn in different ways. Our approach to SEND starts with getting to know your child – their strengths, interests, needs and aspirations – and then adapting teaching and support so they can participate, achieve and feel successful.
If you are considering Ainslie Wood and your child has SEND, we'd be very happy to talk to you and arrange a visit.
Our Vision
At Ainslie Wood Primary School, we are committed to creating an inclusive environment where every child is valued, supported and encouraged to achieve their full potential.
To be a school where every child – regardless of their starting point, background or need – belongs, thrives and is empowered to achieve their personal best.
We believe that every child deserves high-quality teaching, positive relationships and the opportunity to succeed. We work closely with families and outside professionals to ensure that children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) receive the support they need to flourish both academically and personally.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ainslie Wood Primary School - After School Club
pageCache.text:
After School Club
After School Club
We run After School Club from the end of the school day (3:20/3:30) until 6pm. The cost is £14 per child per day, with a reduction for siblings of £11 per day. Pupil Premium children also receive a reduced price of £11 per day.
During After School club, the children will have an afternoon snack and take part in structured games and activities.
You can collect your child from the club by using the After School Club entrance (on the car park side of the school) any time up to 6pm.
Please download the forms and hand them into the school office if you'd like to apply for a place at our After School Club.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ainslie Wood Primary School - How We Support Pupils with SEND
pageCache.text:
How We Support Pupils with SEND
At Ainslie Wood Primary School, we support children across the four broad areas of need identified in the SEND Code of Practice.
Cognition and Learning Some children experience difficulties with learning, memory, processing information, reading, writing or mathematics. We provide carefully planned teaching and targeted interventions to help children develop the knowledge and skills needed to make progress.
Communication and Interaction Some children may experience difficulties understanding language, expressing themselves or communicating with others. This includes children with speech and language needs and autistic children. We provide structured support to develop communication, social interaction and language skills.
Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) Some children may need support to manage their emotions, behaviour, friendships or mental wellbeing. We provide nurturing environments and interventions that help children develop emotional regulation, resilience and positive relationships.
Sensory and/or Physical Needs Some children have physical disabilities, medical needs or sensory processing differences that affect their learning and participation. We work to ensure that reasonable adjustments are made so that every child can access all aspects of school life.
Every child at Ainslie Wood Primary School benefits from Quality First Teaching, where lessons are carefully adapted to meet individual needs.
All pupils are encouraged to participate fully in school life, including:
Where additional support is required, pupils may also receive targeted interventions alongside classroom teaching.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ainslie Wood Primary School - Macmillan Coffee Morning - Friday 26th September
pageCache.text:
Macmillan Coffee Morning - Friday 26th September
We’re delighted to let you know that we’ll once again be taking part in the Macmillan World’s Biggest Coffee Morning on Friday 26th September, from 9am – 10am in the Small Hall.
We’d love your support! Cake Donations – We kindly ask for donations of homemade or shop-bought cakes to sell. Please make sure all cakes are nut-free.
If you’re able to provide gluten-free options, they will be very much appreciated too. Donations should be brought in by Thursday 25th September (morning at the latest).
Join Us - Come along, enjoy coffee and cake with our team, and help us raise money for this important cause.
After-School Cake Sale - Any cakes that don’t get sold in the morning will be available to buy after school on Friday. We hope to see as many of you as possible — everyone is welcome!

Reception Tours
Reception Visits – September to November 2026
We are pleased to offer Reception visits for families considering Ainslie Wood Primary School for September 2027.
Our Reception visits will take place from September to November, giving prospective families the opportunity to look around our school, see our Reception provision and find out more about life at Ainslie Wood.
To ensure that each visit is a welcoming and informative experience, we can accommodate a maximum of 4 families (up to 8 people) per session.
📅 Please see the dates and times below.
Places are limited and must be booked in advance by contacting the school office.
We look forward to welcoming you to Ainslie Wood Primary School!

pageCache.pageTitle: Ainslie Wood Primary School - Red Nose Day - Friday 21st March - Dress Up Day
pageCache.text:
Red Nose Day - Friday 21st March - Dress Up Day
We will be celebrating Comic Relief on Friday 21st March 2025 with a fabulous Back to the 80s theme! We invite all children to come to school wearing their best 1980s outfits. They can wear anything inspired by the 80s, such as leg-warmers, neon colours, big hair and denim jackets! We would be very grateful if you are able to donate £1. All donations raised will go towards Comic Relief to help those in need across the UK and beyond. All children will be encouraged to take part in activities throughout the day, making it as enjoyable as possible. We look forward to seeing everyone in their outfits!
